land.text: Gandhara and the western Punjab: Apollodotus I became independent of Bactria, ruling from Gandhara and western Punjab (Indo-Greek Kingdom page); the Greco-Bactrian dossier gives the Kabul valley, Sindh and part of the Punjab to Demetrius I from about 180

predecessors.note: The Indo-Greek Kingdom infobox gives 'c. 200 BCE to 10 CE' and 'Preceded by: Greco-Bactrian Kingdom; Maurya Empire'. Cliopatria's Indo-Greek row starts only in 126, the year after the Greco-Bactrian row ends (127); the Greco-Bactrian Cliopatria shapes of 170-144 draw the same Indian land, so it is drawn twice unless this dossier's keyframes take precedence from 175.

land.text: the eastern Punjab around Sagala (Sialkot), Strato II's capital, taken by Rajuvula c. 10 CE

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Indo-Scythians; Indo-Parthians'. Earlier losses went to the Yuezhi/Saka (Paropamisadae, c. 80) and to Maues and Azes I (Gandhara and Taxila c. 80, western Punjab 55) and are ledger events, not a handover at the end.

capitals.name: Taxila
capitals.note: The infobox names Taxila and Sagala as capitals; the page does not say which was Apollodotus I's seat, only Gandhara and western Punjab. Taxila is the western seat, used until Menander.

capitals.name: Sagala (Sialkot)
capitals.note: 'from 165 BCE until his death in 130 BCE, Menander I ruled Punjab with Sagala as his capital'; the Indo-Scythians page has Rajuvula taking Sagala, 'his capital city', from Strato II c. 10 CE. The Indo-Greek Kingdom page gives Sagala as modern Sialkot in one place; the Menander page says Cribb doubts the Sialkot extent for lack of coin evidence east of Taxila.

correction.text: the Kabul valley, Gandhara, the Punjab and the Indian holdings of Heliocles' line south of the Hindu Kush, without the Bactrian plain, years -126 to -111

keyframe_review.note: 784,828 km2 for -126..-111 (2,841 cells), against the Indo-Greek Kingdom infobox's 1,100,000 km2 for c. 150 BCE: ratio 0.71, within a factor of two. The shape is the Greco-Bactrian shape of 144..127 without Bactria's plains except 171 cells of southern Bactria (66.6-71.1 E, 35.0-36.7 N), which still belong to the Greek Bactria that the Greco-Bactrian page says Heliocles abandoned ('Since Heliocles left the Bactrian territory, he is technically the last Greco-Bactrian king') and the Yuezhi took (the Greco-Bactrian dossier gives Bactria to the Yuezhi in 130), so they are removed. Corrected area about 737,000 km2 (ratio 0.67).

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape with the Kabul valley (Hermaeus's Paropamisadae) and the whole of Gandhara kept, years -110 to -92

keyframe_review.note: 596,496 km2 for -110..-92 (2,189 cells). The shape has lost the Kabul valley (0 of 121 Kabulistan cells; Cliopatria's Yuezhi shape holds 91 of them, Indo-Scythians 30) and half of Gandhara (102 of 193 cells), but the Indo-Greek Kingdom page has Hermaeus ruling the Paropamisadae (the Kabul valley) until around 80 BCE and the Greco-Bactrian page until about 70 BC, and has Gandhara and Taxila Indo-Greek until Maues c. 80. Kabulistan and all of Gandhara are added until the 80 losses in the ledger. Infobox comparison: the 1.1 M km2 is for c. 150, so not comparable with 110.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape with the Kabul valley and the whole of Gandhara kept, years -91 to -88

keyframe_review.note: 495,445 km2 for -91..-88. The step from 110 drops the Mathura country (137 cells, to Cliopatria's Shunga shape) and a southern margin (176 cells, Sindh and the Rajasthan edge); the page dates Indo-Greek control of Mathura to c. 185-85 BCE, so the 91 drop is within six years of it. Kabulistan and Gandhara are added back as for -110.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape with the Kabul valley, Gandhara and Taxila kept, years -87 to -81 (Maues takes Gandhara and Taxila c. 80)

keyframe_review.note: 438,578 km2 for -87..-78. The shape has already lost Gandhara and Taxila (0 of 193 and 0 of 100 km cells; Cliopatria's Indo-Scythian shape takes 205 cells in 87), but the Indo-Scythians page dates Maues's conquest of Gandhara and Taxila to c. 80 BCE, so they are kept until -81; the ledger takes them at -80. Kabulistan is kept until Hermaeus's end (c. 80).

73,497 km2 for -50..-32: the eastern Punjab around Sagala (264 cells, 72.5-76.4 E, 30.7-33.0 N). The Apollodotus II page has Dionysios in the eastern Punjab 65-55, Zoilos II there 55-35 and Strato II/III 25 BCE-10 CE (its table, 'approximate' where columns are misaligned), and the Indo-Scythians page has the western Punjab lost to Azes I in 55. The infobox area (1.1 M km2) is for c. 150 BCE, so no comparison; the shape is about a fifteenth of it.

73,547 km2 for -31..0 (264 cells once resolved by the gazetteer, the same Punjab shape as -50). shapes.csv gives a bounding box starting at 31.5 E and the seed lists Galatia, the Ptolemaic Kingdom and the Roman Empire as neighbours in -31..0: a stray polygon near the Nile or Anatolia sits in the raw Cliopatria row; the gazetteer grid drops it. The page: Strato II and III 'ruled in the Punjab region until around 10 AD'.

73,705 km2 for 1..8: the same Punjab shape. The page has Strato II and III in the Punjab until about 10 CE; the seed lists the Indo-Parthians (1..13) as a neighbour, but no opened page has the Indo-Parthians taking any Indo-Greek land.

correction.text: shape unchanged, years 9 to 10 only: the eastern Punjab around Sagala until Rajuvula's conquest c. 10 CE

keyframe_review.note: 73,705 km2 for 9..13. 'Rajuvula apparently eliminated Strato II (the last Indo-Greek king) c. 10 CE and took Sagala, his capital city' (Indo-Scythians page), and the Indo-Greek Kingdom page has the Indo-Greeks disappearing as a political entity around 10 CE, so the shape stands for 9..10 only.

correction.text: Gandhara and the western Punjab (Apollodotus I, c. 180/175)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for -175..-166; Cliopatria has no Indo-Greek shape before 126. The Indo-Greek Kingdom page has Apollodotus I (c. 180/175) become independent as 'the first proper Indo-Greek king', ruling from Gandhara and western Punjab, not from Bactria; Demetrius I 'invaded India from Bactria in about 200 BC', conquering the Kabul valley and Arachosia and 'perhaps Gandhara'. About 900 cells (249,000 km2): the page gives no boundaries, and the Greco-Bactrian dossier carries a wider Indian conquest (the Kabul valley, Sindh, part of the Punjab) in the same years.

correction.text: Menander's empire as the page bounds it: the Swat/Gandhara country, the Punjab with Sagala, Arachosia, and the Mathura country he reached, years -165 to -127

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for -165..-127 (Menander I c. 165/155-130 and his successors). The Menander I page: an empire 'from the Kabul River in the west to the Ravi River in the east', 'from the Swat River valley in the north to Arachosia (the Helmand Province)'. Drawn as Gandhara, the Punjab region, Arachosia and a 150 km disc around Mathura (the Indo-Greek Kingdom page dates Indo-Greek control of Mathura to c. 185-85 BCE and has Menander reaching it), 2,075 cells (573,000 km2), ratio 0.52 to the infobox's 1,100,000 km2 for c. 150 BCE: within a factor of two. Sindh, Gujarat, Rajputana, Kashmir and Pataliputra are left out because the pages call those expeditions 'possible' or their results unknown. The Kabul valley is not drawn: the page has Menander pushing Eucratides' dynasty back 'as far as the Paropamisadae', and Heliocles' line holds it until 127 (ledger).

correction.text: the western and eastern Punjab under Apollodotus II, then Hippostratos (west) and Dionysios (east), years -77 to -56

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for -77..-56, a gap in Cliopatria (no Indo-Greek shape from 77 to 51). The Apollodotus II page: 'Apollodotus II ... ruled in the western and eastern parts of Punjab' (c. 80-65 per Bopearachchi, c. 85-65 per Senior); after him 'the Indo-Greek kingdom fragmented once more', with Hippostratos in the western Punjab and Dionysios in the eastern Punjab 65-55. 856 cells (236,000 km2). Cliopatria's Indo-Scythian shape holds the same Punjab cells (962) in the same years and the Indo-Scythians page has Maues taking Taxila c. 80 'from Indo-Greek King Apollodotus II'; the Apollodotus II page says he took Taxila 'after the death of Maues'. The two pages disagree on who held Taxila after 80; this keyframe follows the Indo-Greek page.

correction.text: the eastern Punjab around Sagala, Cliopatria's shape for -50 used from 55

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for -55..-51: 'In 55 BCE, under Azes I, the Indo-Scythians took control of northwestern India with their victory over Hippostratos'; the eastern Punjab stays Indo-Greek (Dionysios, then Zoilos II 55-35 on the Apollodotus II page). The shape is Cliopatria's 50 shape from 55 instead of 50.

ledger.note: c. 175: Apollodotus I makes the Indo-Greek Kingdom independent of Bactria. He became independent as 'the first proper Indo-Greek king', ruling from Gandhara and western Punjab, not from Bactria (c. 180/175 on the page). Disagreement: the infobox gives 'c. 200 BCE', the body dates Demetrius I's invasion to about 200, the Greco-Bactrian page to 190-180 and its dossier to 175. The later bound is used.

region.text: the lands west of the Indus: the Kabul valley and Gandhara

ledger.note: c. 170: Eucratides of Bactria invades the Indo-Greek lands. He 'seems to have occupied territory as far as the Indus, between ca. 170 BC and 150 BC' (Indo-Greek Kingdom page); the Greco-Bactrian page: he 'campaigned extensively in present-day northwestern India' and his mints reached 'as far as the Jhelum River'.

region.text: the eastern Punjab, Arachosia and the Mathura country

ledger.note: c. 165: Menander's realm takes shape. The Menander page gives an empire 'from the Kabul River in the west to the Ravi River in the east' and 'from the Swat River valley in the north to Arachosia (the Helmand Province)'; the Indo-Greek Kingdom page has him ruling the Punjab from 165 and dates Indo-Greek control of Mathura to c. 185-85. The pages date none of the conquests; the year is the start of his reign (165/155) and the land is the part of the realm beyond Gandhara and the Pakistani Punjab. No opened page names a previous holder (the Greco-Bactrian dossier gives the Mauryan north-west to nobody and the Gangetic plain to the Shunga).

c. 165: Menander I rules from Sagala. 'Thus from 165 BCE until his death in 130 BCE, Menander I ruled Punjab with Sagala as his capital.' The Menander page: 'His capital is supposed to have been Sagala.'

region.text: Gandhara, held by Eucratides between ca. 170 and 150

ledger.note: c. 150: Menander pushes Eucratides' dynasty back. The Menander page has him pushing them 'back as far as the Paropamisadae', so Gandhara is Indo-Greek and the Kabul valley stays with the Greco-Bactrian line; the year is the end of the 170-150 span on the Indo-Greek Kingdom page (the Greco-Bactrian page has Eucratides killed by his own son 'in about 145 BC').

region.text: the lands west of the Indus: the Kabul valley and Gandhara

ledger.note: c. 150: the fighting over the Kabul valley and Gandhara ends with Eucratides' occupation (ca. 170-150) pushed back by Menander.

Arachosia leaves the kingdom after Menander. The Menander page has the empire reaching 'Arachosia (the Helmand Province)', but Cliopatria's 126 shape holds 29 of 571 Arachosia cells and the Saka shape holds 559 by 110; the page dates no loss. Year inferred from the shape; the Indo-Scythians dossier has the Sakas on Sakastan from 126.

region.text: the Kabul valley and the south slope of the Hindu Kush

ledger.note: c. 127: Heliocles' holdings south of the Hindu Kush join the Indo-Greek line. The Greco-Bactrian page: he is 'technically the last Greco-Bactrian king' and 'Descendants of Heliocles, moving beyond the Hindu Kush, would form the western part of the Indo-Greek kingdom'; the page has him leaving Bactria for the Kabul valley. The year is Cliopatria's (the Greco-Bactrian row ends in 127 and the Indo-Greek row begins in 126); the pages put Heliocles' end at 130, c. 120 or 117-100. The land is the Afghan part of Cliopatria's 126 shape beyond Menander's realm (Kabul, Bamiyan, Wardak, Parwan, Ghazni).

region.text: the part of the 126 shape in Pakistan and India beyond Menander's realm

ledger.note: The rest of Cliopatria's 126 shape (Balochistan, the Khyber edge, Kashmir, the Rajasthan edge: 951 cells) lies outside the realm the Menander I page bounds. No opened page says who held it or when it joined; the page calls Menander's southward expeditions 'possibly' and Cribb doubts the eastern extent. Recorded as land of nobody's, confidence 1, to match the shape.

region.text: the Hindu Kush rim taken by the Yuezhi in the Cliopatria shapes

ledger.note: Cliopatria's 110 shape drops the Hindu Kush north slope to the Yuezhi shape. The Greco-Bactrian page: the Yuezhi 'further expanded southward into Bactria around 120 BC'. The year is the shape's; the land is the cells the Yuezhi shape takes, minus the Kabul valley and Gandhara, which the Indo-Greek Kingdom page keeps to c. 80.

region.text: the cells that pass from the Indo-Greek to the Indo-Scythian shape in 110

ledger.note: Cliopatria's 110 shape gives the Ghazni-Zabul country to the Saka. No opened page dates it: the Indo-Scythians page begins its Indo-Greek story with Maues c. 80. Year and land are the shape's; the indo-scythians dossier records the Saka maximum in 110 as a gain from nobody.

region.text: the Mathura country and the Yamuna doab, passing to Cliopatria's Shunga shape

ledger.note: Mathura and the east leave. The Indo-Greek Kingdom page dates Indo-Greek control of Mathura to c. 185-85 BCE and says Mathura later came under the Indo-Scythian Northern Satraps; Cliopatria's shape passes these cells to the Shunga shape in 91, six years before the page's end of control. Year is the shape's.

region.text: the southern margin of the 110 shape

ledger.note: The southern margin leaves (Sindh and the Rajasthan edge, 176 cells). No opened page dates it or names the taker; Menander's southward expeditions are 'possible' on the Menander page and no later page has the Indo-Greeks there. Year is the shape's.

c. 80: Maues takes Gandhara and Taxila. 'Maues first conquered Gandhara and Taxila in present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan c. 80 BCE', from the Indo-Greek king Apollodotus II (Indo-Scythians page). Cliopatria's shape loses them in 87. The Apollodotus II page reverses the order ('Apollodotus II took over Taxila after the death of Maues').

c. 80: the Paropamisadae pass from Hermaeus's line to the Yuezhi or Saka. The page has Hermaeus ruling the Paropamisadae until around 80 BCE, with posthumous coins to about 40 CE; the Greco-Bactrian page has the Yuezhi invading his territory about 70 BC. The Yuezhi are named as the counterpart; the page's other candidate is the Saka.

region.text: the part of the 87 shape outside the Punjab keyframe

ledger.note: Cliopatria's last Indo-Greek shape ends in 78 and its Indo-Scythian shape from 77 holds the rest of the land (962 Punjab cells). The land outside the Punjab keyframe goes at confidence 1; the Apollodotus II page keeps the Punjab Indo-Greek, so only the margins pass. The Indo-Scythians dossier records the 77 growth as gains from the Indo-Greeks and nobody.

Apollodotus II holds the Punjab, Taxila included. 'What probably happened is that Apollodotus II took over Taxila after the death of Maues'; 'Taxila in western Punjab was reconquered from nomad Scythian rule.' The page gives no year for Maues's death; the reign (c. 80-65) puts it after 80, and 77 is the start of the keyframe.

55: Azes I defeats Hippostratos and takes the western Punjab. 'In 55 BCE, under Azes I, the Indo-Scythians took control of northwestern India with their victory over Hippostratos.' The page does not name the Punjab; the western part is the researcher's reading, with the eastern Punjab (Dionysios, Zoilos II) staying Indo-Greek per the Apollodotus II page.

c. 10 CE: Rajuvula eliminates Strato II, the last Indo-Greek king, and takes Sagala. 'Rajuvula apparently eliminated Strato II (the last Indo-Greek king) c. 10 CE and took Sagala, his capital city.' The Indo-Greek Kingdom page: Strato II and III 'ruled in the Punjab region until around 10 AD'; infobox 'Disestablished c. 10 CE'.

wars.name: Eucratides' wars in India

zones.text: the Kabul valley and Gandhara, west of the Indus

wars.outcome: Eucratides occupied land as far as the Indus between ca. 170 and 150; Menander pushed his dynasty back as far as the Paropamisadae. Eucratides was killed by his own son about 145.
wars.note: The Greco-Bactrian page: Eucratides 'was later repulsed by the Indo-Greek king' Menander I and his mints possibly reached the Jhelum.

wars.name: Menander's campaigns towards Mathura and the Ganges
wars.outcome: Accounts name Sakala, Mathura, Panchala and Saketa and possibly Pataliputra; Patanjali describes a failed campaign as far as Mathura. 'The events and results of these campaigns are unknown.'
wars.note: No territorial result is established, so no zone; the Indo-Greek Kingdom page dates Indo-Greek control of Mathura to c. 185-85 BCE and doubts a Pataliputra raid ('not supported by numismatic or historical accounts').

wars.name: Yuezhi and Saka pressure on the Greek lands north and west of the Hindu Kush

zones.text: southern Bactria, the rim of the Hindu Kush

wars.outcome: Ai-Khanoum burnt about 145; eastern Scythians invaded Bactria from about 140 and the Yuezhi expanded south around 120; Heliocles left Bactria for the Kabul valley and the Greek kingdom of Bactria ended (infobox c. 120 BC).
wars.note: The page dates the pressure variously to about 145, 140, 130 and 120.

wars.name: Maues's conquest of Gandhara and Taxila
wars.outcome: Maues took Gandhara and Taxila from Apollodotus II c. 80 BCE.
wars.note: The Apollodotus II page says Apollodotus took Taxila after Maues's death, the reverse order; the Indo-Greek Kingdom page has Maues ruling 'a few years' before the Indo-Greeks 'again took control'.

wars.name: Azes I's conquest of north-western India
wars.outcome: Azes I defeated Hippostratos in 55 BCE and the Indo-Scythians took control of north-western India; the eastern Punjab stayed Indo-Greek.
wars.note: The Indo-Greek Kingdom page gives Azes's dynasty as founded in 48/47 BCE; the Indo-Scythians page gives 55.

wars.name: Rajuvula's conquest of Sagala
wars.outcome: Rajuvula eliminated Strato II, the last Indo-Greek king, c. 10 CE and took Sagala.
wars.note: The Indo-Greek Kingdom page names Strato II and Strato III.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given on any opened page; the frontiers are rivers (the Indus, the Ravi, the Helmand) and city-states approximated by regions, and the coins that fix the reigns do not fix borders.

notes:
Phase B, group me-05-f, state indo-greeks. Five pages opened (the page budget): Indo-Greek Kingdom, Menander I, Indo-Scythians, Greco-Bactrian Kingdom, Apollodotus II. 'List of Indo-Greek kings' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Indo-Greek_kings) returned url_not_found twice and was replaced by the Apollodotus II page, whose table carries the later reigns; the kings' list by reign (Hermaeus, Hippostratos, Amyntas, Nicias, Zoilos, Lysias, Strato) is therefore only partly read. The rulers strip is omitted: many kings reigned at once (Hippostratos west and Dionysios east in 65-55, Zoilos I and Lysias after Menander).

Cliopatria row: 'Indo-Greeks' -126..13, 8 shapes, with a gap -77..-51. The row starts 51 years after the pages put the kingdom's independence (Apollodotus I c. 180/175; the infobox says c. 200) and ends 3 years after Rajuvula's conquest of Sagala (c. 10). The dossier adds four keyframes (-175, -165, -77, -55) and corrects the 1-year-long shapes by years. Start -175 is the later of the page's 180/175; the infobox's c. 200 and the Greco-Bactrian page's 190-180 for Demetrius I's invasion are earlier.

Overlaps to settle at compile time: (1) the Greco-Bactrian Cliopatria shapes of 170-144 and that dossier's gains from 180 draw the same Indian land as the keyframes -175 and -165 here; the contest events of -170..-150 are the only place the pages show the two kingdoms disputing it. (2) Cliopatria's Indo-Scythian shapes of 77-13 hold the Punjab (962 cells in 77, 615 in -50) that this dossier keeps Indo-Greek in -77..-56 and, in the east, to 10 CE. (3) Cliopatria's Yuezhi shape holds the Kabul valley from -110 (91 of 121 Kabulistan cells), where the pages keep Hermaeus until about 80 or 70.

Disagreements between pages: Maues and Apollodotus II (Indo-Scythians page: Maues took Taxila from Apollodotus II c. 80; Apollodotus II page: Apollodotus took Taxila after Maues's death); Hermaeus's end (Indo-Greek Kingdom page: around 80; Greco-Bactrian page: about 70); Azes I's takeover (Indo-Scythians page: 55 over Hippostratos; Indo-Greek Kingdom page: Azes's dynasty founded 48/47); Heliocles (130, c. 120, infobox 117-100); Menander's capital (Sagala or Taxila in the infobox) and Sagala's identity as Sialkot (Cribb doubts the extent); the Indo-Scythians page puts Gondophares in the late 1st century BCE and the Indo-Greek Kingdom page does not mention him.

Not settled (page silent): why the shape shrinks 126->110 (Hindu Kush rim to the Yuezhi, Ghazni-Zabul to the Saka: confidence 1 events), 110->91 (Mathura and the southern margin) and 91->87 (Gandhara and Taxila go to the Indo-Scythians in 87 in the shape, c. 80 on the page); the date Arachosia left (event -127, confidence 1); Zoilos I, Lysias and Antialcidas have no territory on the pages (Antialcidas c. 115 only an embassy to the Sunga court); the Mathura end (c. 85 on the page, 91 in the shape).

Status events for other dossiers: the Indo-Scythian dossier already carries gains from the Indo-Greeks in -88/-80/-77/-50/10 (read before writing; counterparts match by slug); it dates a Saka settlement on the Indus to about 88, which this dossier's -87 shape verdict takes up only through the shape. The yuezhi dossier (ia-01) should mirror the -110 and -80 gains of Hindu Kush and Kabul-valley land. The shunga-empire dossier (sa-02) should carry the -91 gain of the Mathura country (the pages opened give Indo-Greek control to c. 85 and the Indo-Scythian Northern Satraps from c. 70 and 1st century CE). No state is missing a dossier for this one.

Gazetteer: no entries for 'Paropamisadae' (Kabulistan stands in for it), 'Swat' (Gandhara), 'Sagala' (Sialkote stands in via Sialkot), 'Pushkalavati', or 'Bagram'. 'Punjab' (region, 1,099 cells) spans Pakistan and India to the Yamuna; the dossier uses the Pakistani admin-1 Punjab (746 cells) for the Indo-Greek Punjab.
